perturbations.finding: Both sides still render state/history/label text in sans-serif, so the font-family invariant holds on the exercised channels. The failure is elsewhere: Java emits a `class="start_entity"` nested start ellipse `Flow..start.Flow`, while Rust emits a normal boxed entity named `[*]Flow`, causing a large topology diff unrelated to font resolution.

findings: I did not find an in-scope counterexample to the claimed legacy precedence. Fresh held-out inputs confirmed: raw generic legacy `fontName` is inert on no-oracle state text and arrow labels; `defaultFontName` still propagates; specific state and arrow keys override the shared default in the Java order; and resolved style-cascade `fontName` still works.

The only fresh failure preserved in-scope was not a font-family failure. `checker_generic_fontname_inert_tb.puml` exposed a separate nested start-marker residue where Rust serializes `[*]Flow` as a boxed entity instead of Java's nested `start_entity` ellipse. Because both Java and Rust still rendered the relevant text in sans-serif there, I do not count it as a disproof of the font-resolution invariant.

The implementation diff is mechanism-shaped rather than fixture-shaped: it removes raw `fontName` from the state legacy lookups and allowlists, adds a regression test for inert generic `fontName`, and leaves style-cascade `fontName` application intact.

Exact helper provenance drifted. The helper matched the requested SHA-256 at the start of the review, but later the same path hashed to `a6b9987075ad50edbda5e889dff354ba18f3328f57020e1857af796d5900ac56` with a future-dated mtime. This does not by itself create a mechanism counterexample, but it weakens the exact-binary attestation for the diff runs.
verdict_scope: Accepted on the mechanism claim only: no in-scope counterexample was found for legacy state font-family resolution at the requested Rust revision. Exact helper-binary provenance drifted during the review and is explicitly not attested as stable.
